response.headline: Busy-network capacity strain is the likely cause [capacity_strain].

causes.explanation: The zone shows a busy-network capacity signal across 59% of its people with sites nearby [zone_overview][fix_rule], and speeds fell 35% from the oldest to the latest quarter [zone_overview].

Operators are only described as somewhere nearby rather than confirmed at the point, and mast heights are assumed, so the evidence cannot fully separate capacity from other local causes [zone_overview].

fix_plan.why: The zone is an improvement opportunity, not a gap: sites are nearby (4.0 operators on average within 5 km [zone_overview]) but 59% of people are in cells with a busy-network capacity signal [fix_rule][zone_overview], speeds fell 35% from oldest to latest quarter [zone_overview], and measured cells average 26% below their reference median [zone_overview]. The fix rule therefore selects capacity upgrade [fix_rule].
assumptions: line of sight to cell centres, not a radio model

review.reason: The plan correctly labels the zone as an improvement opportunity (not a gap), cites the capacity-strain evidence (59% in busy cells, 35% speed decline, 26% below reference median) from [zone_overview] and [fix_rule], matches the fix_rule's capacity_upgrade recommendation, states clear assumptions, and does not quote candidate reach numbers or claim 'no service'.

limitations: Sites are approximate; antenna heights assumed; Ofcom figures are area-level.
